questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a concern if no passengers are getting off.
Should not be on the road.
Is always a concern, whether you see passengers or not.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is always a concern, whether you see passengers or not.
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around a stopped bus. Passengers may walk in front of or behind it. The bus may also block their view of your vehicle.

questions.question: To park as safely as possible, you should:

options.text: Park so you must back up to leave.
Park so you can pull forward to leave.
Park on the side of the road, not in a lot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park so you can pull forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous. Avoid it when possible. Park so you can pull forward to exit your space.

questions.question: An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph in ideal conditions needs approximately ____ to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle at 55 mph in ideal conditions needs about 450 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: Foundation brakes are used:

options.text: Only at the driver's side wheels.

questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are located at all four wheels. The most common type is the S-cam drum brake.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what is the best way to check your lights?

options.text: Park near a mirror and look for a reflection.
Turn on the lights, then get out and look at them.
Check the instrument panel for warning lights.
Drive in traffic and wait for other drivers to signal if your lights are out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the lights, then get out and look at them.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, turn on your lights and exit the vehicle to visually inspect them.

questions.question: Which exhaust system problems should be fixed?
questions.explanation: Exhaust system problems are serious because poisonous fumes can enter the cab. Fix loose, broken, or missing parts; parts rubbing against other components; and leaking parts.

questions.question: Where is the safety relief valve usually located?
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve in an air brake system is located in the first air tank to receive air from the compressor.

questions.question: A vehicle should have all of the following, except:

options.text: Warning devices for parked vehicles, like flares.

questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must carry proper emergency equipment: at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless the vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles such as triangles, flares, or fuses.

questions.question: A driver should always:
questions.explanation: Always scan the road ahead to spot hazards early. Plan how you will respond if a hazard becomes dangerous.

questions.question: What can happen if you use the parking brake in wet weather below freezing?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and prevent the vehicle from moving.
The brakes may suddenly release on their own.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and prevent the vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: Using the parking brake in very wet, freezing conditions can cause the brakes to freeze, making the vehicle unable to move.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most heavy-duty vehicles use?
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems for safety.

questions.question: How can you help others see your vehicle?

options.text: Turn headlights off during the day.
Use headlights only when it rains.

questions.explanation: Clean headlights provide more light at night. This helps other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.question: What does the service brake system do?

options.text: It applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving normally.
It applies and releases the parking brakes.
It applies and releases the emergency brake.
It applies and releases the axle brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving normally.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three separate braking systems. The service brake system applies and releases the brakes when you use the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: What happens when brakes fade while driving down a steep hill?

options.text: They work differently from front to back.

questions.explanation: Using brakes too much on a steep downhill can overheat them. Overheated brakes become less effective. Use engine braking to avoid this problem.

questions.question: When inspecting the exhaust system, which is NOT a problem?

options.text: Exhaust system parts that are not rubbing against fuel system parts

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts that are not rubbing against fuel system parts
questions.explanation: When inspecting the exhaust system, watch for loose, broken, or missing pipes; loose mounting brackets; and leaking parts. Exhaust parts should never rub against fuel system parts, tires, or other moving parts.

questions.question: For a first railroad-highway grade crossing violation, your CDL will be suspended for at least ____.
questions.explanation: A first violation for crossing a railroad-highway grade crossing will result in losing your CDL for at least 60 days.

questions.question: How much water on the road surface is needed for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: A lot, like a large puddle

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip with the road and slide on water. Even a small amount of water on the road can cause hydroplaning.

questions.question: During the pre-trip inspection, when you start the vehicle, the coolant temperature should:
questions.explanation: After starting your vehicle, watch the gauges. The coolant temperature should gradually rise to its normal operating temperature.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, increase the space in front of your vehicle so the other driver can pass safely. Driving faster is dangerous because the tailgater may speed up too, making the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Remove your foot from the brake pedal.
Turn quickly in the direction of the skid.
Countersteer after the vehicle is back on course.

questions.explanation: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, lift your foot from the brake so locked wheels can roll again. Quickly steer in the direction you want to go. Then countersteer to prevent skidding in the opposite direction. Do not accelerate.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Brake harder than you would in a vehicle without ABS.
Use extra braking force to make the ABS activate.
Brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
Brake with less force than you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way whether your vehicle has ABS or not. ABS works automatically to help you stop safely.

questions.question: When can brakes get out of adjustment?
questions.explanation: Brakes can quickly go out of adjustment when they overheat from heavy use. Check your brakes often.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Shoes with oil or grease on them
Pads with no oil or grease on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads with no oil or grease on them
questions.explanation: Bad brake signs include cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are worn too thin. Clean pads without oil or grease are fine.

questions.question: What is true about pull-ups during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: A pull-up always counts against you.
You must do at least one pull-up.
Stopping without changing direction is not a pull-up.
Some test examiners think too many pull-ups are okay.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping without changing direction is not a pull-up.
questions.explanation: A pull-up happens when you stop and then move forward to get a better position. Just stopping is not a pull-up. Too many pull-ups will count as mistakes.

questions.question: What can improperly loaded cargo do?

options.text: Look bad to other drivers on the road.
Injure the driver during a quick stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Injure the driver during a quick stop.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be loaded and tied down properly so it does not move or fall. During a quick stop, loose cargo can hurt or kill the driver.

questions.question: When do spring brakes come on?

options.text: When air pressure drops too much.
When a dashboard control is turned on.
When tires have very little tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops too much.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes turn on automatically when air pressure gets too low. Do not wait for this to happen. If you see the low pressure warning, pull over safely and stop while you still have brake control.

questions.question: What is required to get a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: Submit your fingerprints and have a background check done.
Submit your fingerprints only if you had a traffic violation in the last three years.
Have a background check only if you had a traffic violation in the last three years.

questions.correctAnswerText: Submit your fingerprints and have a background check done.
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must submit your fingerprints and pass a background check.

questions.question: What is a good rule when making a turn?

options.text: Use your arms to get other drivers' attention.
Turn off your turn signal before entering the turn so you do not confuse other drivers.

questions.explanation: Signal well ahead of time so drivers behind you know you are turning. Keep your signal on during the turn and turn it off after the turn is complete.

questions.question: What can cause hydraulic brakes to fail?

options.text: Driving uphill for a long time.

questions.explanation: Hydraulic brakes usually fail when they lose pressure. They can also fail from overheating when used heavily on long downhill drives.

questions.question: During the driving skills test, if you pass under an overpass, what might the examiner ask you to recall?

options.text: If there was a shoulder near the roadway.

questions.explanation: Your examiner may ask you to recall the posted clearance or height of an overpass you drove under during the on-road driving skills test.

questions.question: How do you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Turn the parking brake on and off.
Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
Disconnect and reconnect all air hoses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the system has charged, test the warning signal by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air from the brakes. The warning signal should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: A distracted driver usually:

options.text: Is aware of what is happening around them.
Is a good person to follow.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving slows your perception, delays your decisions, and causes improper actions. Watch for distracted drivers and stay away from them when you can.

questions.question: The suspension system:

options.text: Supports the vehicle and its cargo.
Keeps the cargo at the right distance behind the driver.
Keeps a safe distance between your vehicle and others.
Reduces the weight on the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supports the vehicle and its cargo.
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and cargo while keeping the axles in place. Damage to the suspension system is very dangerous.

questions.question: Before driving in winter, check:
questions.explanation: Before winter driving, check your heating and defrosting systems, coolant and antifreeze levels, wipers and washers, tire tread, tire chains, lights, reflectors, and exhaust system. Remove ice and snow from all windows, mirrors, hand holds, steps, deck plates, and radiator shutters.

questions.question: If a truck's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops working:

options.text: The truck will have no brakes.
The truck should only be driven slowly.
The truck will still have brakes.
The truck will have no brakes on the left side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: If the ABS system fails, the vehicle still has normal brakes. Drive and brake as you normally would.

questions.question: When checking under your vehicle for fluid leaks, look for all of these except:
questions.explanation: Before a trip, look under your vehicle for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test:

options.text: Points are taken off for each pull-up.
A driver can do three pull-ups per maneuver.
A pull-up earns points only if the driver gets out of the vehicle first.
Only too many pull-ups count as errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only too many pull-ups count as errors.
questions.explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, one pull-up is allowed without penalty. However, too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: When you approach your vehicle, make sure:

options.text: The vehicle looks cleaner than others.
The vehicle is not parked too close to other vehicles.
There are no puddles under the vehicle that suggest a leak.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are no puddles under the vehicle that suggest a leak.
questions.explanation: Before inspection, check your vehicle's general condition and make sure it is not damaged or leaning. Look under it for fresh leaks. Check around the vehicle for hazards like people, other vehicles, or low-hanging wires or branches.

questions.question: What is sleep debt?

options.text: Not getting enough sleep over time.
The time needed to get ready after waking up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not getting enough sleep over time.
questions.explanation: You build up a sleep debt when you do not get enough sleep. You can only pay back this debt by getting more sleep.

questions.question: When it is hard for others to see your vehicle at dawn or dusk, you should:

options.text: Wave your arm out the window.

questions.explanation: When visibility is low, turn your headlights to low beam. If you have trouble seeing others, they probably have trouble seeing you too.

questions.question: Which crime would NOT disqualify someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: Several crimes disqualify someone from a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years. These include arson, robbery, and crimes involving dishonesty or fraud. More serious crimes like murder result in a lifetime disqualification.

questions.question: On a truck with air brakes, the air compressor:

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The governor controls the air compressor.

questions.question: How many licenses can a driver have?

options.text: Two licenses, one for automobiles and one for trucks.
A license for each state in which they plan to drive.
An automobile license from one state and a CDL from another.

questions.explanation: A person can only have one license. States share driver information through a computer system to prevent duplicate licenses.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one system has a leak:

options.text: There are always leaks in both systems.
It may not affect the other system.
It will affect the other system.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may not affect the other system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: If your heavy load is slowing you down, you should:

options.text: Keep the vehicle in second gear.

questions.explanation: The right lanes are for slower-moving vehicles. If your heavy load is slowing you down, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: Which of these is most likely to cause hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is most likely on wet roads when tire pressure is low or tread is worn. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph with enough water on the road.

questions.question: When making tight turns, a driver should:

options.text: Open the door for a better view.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. Check them especially when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: Move over laws require:

options.text: Trucks to use the left lane.
All vehicles to leave the lane next to an emergency vehicle with flashing lights that is stopped.
All vehicles to use the left lane.
All vehicles to move to the left lane if a flatbed trailer is in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles to leave the lane next to an emergency vehicle with flashing lights that is stopped.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is stopped on the side of the road, drivers must leave the lane next to it if possible. If you cannot safely move over, slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: If you need to drive in reverse, you should:

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Exit the truck and walk the path to check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.
Stick your head out the window to look backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the truck and walk the path to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out and walk around to check for hazards. Use both mirrors while backing. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: When driving, you should:

options.text: Avoid using mirrors because they are distracting.
Use mirrors only when there is traffic.
Check your mirrors regularly, but only on cloudy days.

questions.explanation: Stay aware of your surroundings at all times. Check your mirrors regularly.
